races.name: Racedays For 9 Pound At Nottingham Racecourse Nursery

runners_data.name: Havana Grey Star
runners_data.note: Three runs in, all on good going at 5f-6f with finishing positions of 8-5-4, showing no wins or places; Tudhope takes over for Hughes and the step to 6f is not untried but the form line offers little encouragement on a track and trip where more progressive rivals dominate.
runners_data.comment: Well below her best at Sandown last time and the trainer's yard has been in a quiet spell recently; her earlier outings suggested more ability over this trip on a sound surface, and a handicap debut can bring out the best — a return to form is possible if she rediscovers that earlier level.

runners_data.name: Ponte Carlo
runners_data.note: Ran third at 7f on standard and third at 5f on soft — the form is mixed — but crucially this horse's true inclination is to race from the rear, and with several similar hold-up types crowding the back end it is unlikely to get a clean run from its preferred position, which must temper expectations regardless of the going suitability.
runners_data.comment: Third by 2 1/4 lengths in a maiden at Newcastle last time, showing he handles a range of trips up to 7f, and he steps into handicap company today wearing first-time cheekpieces; yet to score but the profile suggests there is more to come off a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Invincible Isaac
runners_data.note: A visor goes on for this hold-up type who has finished 10th, 4th, 9th, and 5th in its last four — the headgear change is the key angle to monitor, but the horse's natural trailing style is squeezed by the quantity of hold-up horses in this field and Callan's 3lb claim counts for less when the tactical picture is this congested.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7 lengths in a maiden at Bath last time and needs to show considerably more to get competitive in handicap company; wears a first-time visor today, which is of interest, and handles the trip on good ground — a significant step forward in performance is required.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Back-to-back second-place finishes at 6f on good and soft show genuine consistency at this trip, and Oisin Orr is an upgrade; with OR 70 and a pattern of running on well from off the pace, this is one of the more credible hold-up threats if the pace does stretch.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time cheekpieces, he was a length second in a maiden here last time and clearly handles the course and today's trip; yet to score but has the ability to be competitive, and he could improve again if he builds on that effort.

runners_data.name: Yahaira
runners_data.note: The only runner in the field with a recent 6f win on good ground — that victory came just nine days ago and the quick turnaround could be a factor — headgear was worn previously and the horse has form from off the pace, making it a genuine player if the pace proves generous enough.
runners_data.comment: Landed a narrow win at Newbury last time over 6f on fast ground and brings cheekpieces to add today; with plenty of pace and effective on this surface, she merits respect as a potential improver on her handicap bow.

runners_data.name: Courseyoudo
runners_data.note: Three runs all on good at 5f showing 7th, 5th, 6th — no win or place — and this horse naturally wants to race from the hold-up position, but sits mapped in midfield because the rear is oversubscribed; the step up to 6f for the first time is unexplored territory and the overall profile asks for a leap of faith.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and sits at the foot of our ratings; his latest at Sandown showed marginal forward movement though he may not have beaten much given the long starting price, and a trainer in decent form is the main encouragement as he goes handicapping.

runners_data.name: Ziggy Starshine
runners_data.note: The pace map's linchpin — one win and three places from three runs, all on good ground, with the sole victory coming at 5f and two seconds at 6f; a style-fit flag notes it is mapped slightly out of pure lead role but in practice this is the horse that will set the tempo and its proven ability to dominate on good-to-firm makes it the race's pivotal actor.
runners_data.comment: Useful filly with a win in recent starts; her latest at Wetherby, where she was beaten 2 lengths stepping up slightly in trip, showed she handles a sound surface and the move to 6f looks in her favour — an opening mark of 74 makes her well treated on debut in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Joint top-rated at OR 74 alongside Ziggy Starshine, this Jack Channon-trained juvenile returns from 64 days off having won at 5f and placed at 5f on good ground — the step to 6f is the key unknown, but the class and form profile suggest the longer trip could unlock further improvement on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Landed a maiden success at Pontefract last time by 1 1/4 lengths and looks open to improvement now stepping into handicap company; effective at 5f with 6f a potential further plus, though a break of over two months may need working through.

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy Starshine is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 8-runner 6f nursery and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should stride out uncontested from the gates on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham. That scenario creates a controlled, single-file gallop where the leader dictates tempo — a sustainable pace that suits a horse who has already won at 5f and placed twice at 6f in similar conditions. The hold-up brigade — Koodini, Yahaira, and Ponte Carlo among them — will be riding the slipstream but face the classic problem of a lone front-runner who never truly gets caught cold. This race shape heavily favours the lead-to-prominent profile: a horse who can sit just off a measured pace and produce a clean, uninterrupted finish on fast ground. The field contains significantly more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ponte Carlo, Courseyoudo, and Invincible Isaac are all natural hold-up horses but have been mapped to midfield; Ziggy Starshine and any horse able to track closely are the runners most likely to actually secure the prominent positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ziggy Starshine Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy Starshine breaks cleanly and settles into a measured lead without any rival pressing from the outside.
scenarios.body: If Ziggy Starshine breaks cleanly and settles into a measured lead without any rival pressing from the outside.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy Starshine sets a stronger pace than expected and tires in the final furlong, opening the door for a closer.
scenarios.body: If Ziggy Starshine sets a stronger pace than expected and tires in the final furlong, opening the door for a closer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits just off Ziggy Starshine's shoulder throughout and strikes decisively inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a horse sits just off Ziggy Starshine's shoulder throughout and strikes decisively inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant interference, a slow start by the favourite, or the pace collapses causing a messy finish.
scenarios.body: If there is significant interference, a slow start by the favourite, or the pace collapses causing a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy Starshine's gate start is critical — if it misses the break, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes genuinely open for the hold-up horses behind.

Innichen returns from a 64-day absence for Jack Channon — watch the market for signs of stable confidence, as a well-prepared return over 6f for the first time would make it the chief danger to the pace-setter.

Koodini and Yahaira are both hold-up horses with the most credible recent form at this trip, but they are racing into a shape where the lone front-runner dictates — monitor whether either jockey elects to press closer than their natural position to avoid being left flat-footed.

Ponte Carlo, Courseyoudo, and Invincible Isaac are all true hold-up types mapped forward by necessity — if any of them try to force position early, they risk burning energy out of role and compromising their finish entirely.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for the 2:00 at Nottingham; all three of Ziggy Starshine's runs have been on identical going and the surface suits — any deterioration during the card would be worth noting for the hold-up brigade but appears unlikely today.

runners_data.name: Grey Tamam
runners_data.comment: A 140,000-euro Churchill purchase from the breeze-ups who arrives with real appeal on debut for a yard firing at 32% in recent weeks; her dam excelled over 8f and this filly has the profile to make an immediate impression — commands the most respect in this field.

runners_data.name: Nicely
runners_data.comment: A £95,000 Persian Force purchase from the breeze-ups who has much in her favour as a first-time runner; her dam was a very useful performer over 7f and she is a half-sister to Kazakh, giving her a strong speed pedigree — a filly to take seriously on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Chiwara
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement on debut at Ripon, finishing second beaten 2 lengths over 6f on good ground; already handles the conditions and trip, and a filly with just the one run looks open to further progress second time out — a strong danger in this heat.

runners_data.name: Fairy Well
runners_data.comment: A 180,000gns Dark Angel filly out of a dam that was a very smart performer over 6f as a juvenile, and a full-sister to the useful Rum Therapy over this trip; ranks last on our figures on debut, but the strong pedigree makes her one to keep in mind.

runners_data.name: Ash Tree
runners_data.comment: A 240,000-euro Blue Point filly who is a full sister to Archer Royal, a smart performer over 8f; merits close attention on her debut and, while there is no previous form to judge her by, the profile alone marks her out as a serious contender.

runners_data.name: Bearly Blue
runners_data.comment: Runner-up beaten 4 lengths at Goodwood last time having moved forward from her debut, but today's faster ground is a potential concern given she has shown her best on soft; ranks fifth on our figures and the switch to firmer conditions is a question worth noting.

races.name: Hon. Alderman Malcolm Wood Memorial Nursery

runners_data.name: On The Queue Tee
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for J S Moore and Cieren Fallon, with three runs at 5-6f on Good ground and consistency without winning; reliant on a strong pace developing to get competitive and faces a tactical puzzle here if Past Passion keeps it gentle.
runners_data.comment: Well below her best in a Listed event at Ascot on her latest start, a step up in class that proved beyond her; back to 5f in a handicap is a sounder proposition, though the trainer's recent form is a concern and she has shown inconsistency in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's hold-up filly is a genuine rear-of-field type whose last three finishes read 7-6-3 on similar ground — she carries a STYLE_FIT tag because she is squeezed into a midfield position that is not her natural game, which tempers confidence in her making an impact unless the pace genuinely stretches the field.
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Bath on her most recent outing, a result that showed a step forward in form, and this move into handicap company at 5f looks a positive angle; lightly tried and capable of further progress, she is hard to overlook as a handicap newcomer.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, Rowan Scott can exploit an uncontested lead on fast Nottingham ground; she won on Good and hit the frame on Soft, showing versatility, and her ability to set her own terms is her single biggest asset in this field.
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Ffos Las on her latest start, handling softer conditions there, and the switch to handicap company may help her show more; acts at 5f and has shown promise in recent starts, though today's quicker ground remains an unknown.

runners_data.name: Seed Ya Later
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's highest-rated runner on official figures at OR 69, Edward Greatrex rides and this filly has already won and placed twice at 5f on fast ground, giving her solid course-and-distance form credentials that make her a natural match for a track-the-leader scenario.
runners_data.comment: Third under a penalty at Bath on her latest outing, a result that underlines her soundness in form, and the step into handicap company looks a natural progression for this 5f filly who handles good and firm ground; there is more to come.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: The Quinn yard sends this filly in at OR 68 with a course-and-distance placed run on Good ground last time; a hold-up type who will need the pace to be honest enough to close from the rear — 26 days since her last run and no headgear concerns.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten three-quarters of a length in a seller at Musselburgh on her latest start back on turf, and the handicap switch may unlock something; rated sixth of seven on our figures and needs to step up to feature here.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's OR 80 top-rated, with Jack Callan (3lb claimer) aboard — has won at 5f on Good and finished third on the same track, but his prominent style is perfectly suited here to track Past Passion and produce his effort in the last furlong; Palmer's T14 strike rate of 6/53 is a mild trainer flag but the form profile is strong.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race in recent starts and showed useful ability at 5f on good ground; his latest outing in a visor at Beverley was forgettable, though that run came with excuses, and back to his better form he heads this field on our ratings from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: David Evans's busy operator (12 days since last run, visor fitted) carries OR 78 and a form string packed with places — two wins, four seconds — and J F Egan is an experienced handler of front-foot horses; style is genuinely prominent and the visor may sharpen her focus in a race where alertness at the break matters.
runners_data.comment: Showed smart form when going down by a neck at 5f in a novice contest at Redcar on his latest outing, and heads into his handicap debut in a first-time visor with a trainer operating in good form; the consistent profile makes him a chief rival.

races.paceDynamic: Past Passion is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 5f nursery on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham, and with no rival expected to seriously contest the lead, she is likely to control the pace from the outset at a sustainable tempo that does not burn herself up. Seed Ya Later, Wait Geordie, and Undercover Affair all carry genuine prominent profiles and will press for the early positions just behind, creating a tidy gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching on this flat track. This field actually contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Holi Scarlett is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into the mapped midfield because On The Queue Tee and Havana Gift also hold similar profiles, meaning the back markers will be bunched and reliant on a late gap that an uncontested pace may not open. A controlled, front-running shape on fast ground at Nottingham strongly favours prominent-style runners who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong, rather than those forced to make up ground from a held-up position against a pace that never truly injures itself.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Past Passion dictates a sustainable pace and one of the prominent trio (Seed Ya Later, Wait Geordie, Undercover Affair) travels smoothly in her wake before cutting her down inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Past Passion dictates a sustainable pace and one of the prominent trio (Seed Ya Later, Wait Geordie, Undercover Affair) travels smoothly in her wake before cutting her down inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Past Passion's controlled front-running at an honest but not breakneck pace proves impossible to reel in on fast ground with hold-up horses unable to get competitive.
scenarios.body: If Past Passion's controlled front-running at an honest but not breakneck pace proves impossible to reel in on fast ground with hold-up horses unable to get competitive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough mid-race to string out the field and create genuine late-run opportunities for the hold-up horses tracking from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens enough mid-race to string out the field and create genuine late-run opportunities for the hold-up horses tracking from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Melee, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If prominent horses jostle for position early, disrupting each other's rhythm and creating a compressed finish where no single runner builds a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: If prominent horses jostle for position early, disrupting each other's rhythm and creating a compressed finish where no single runner builds a decisive advantage.

watchPoints.text: Past Passion (Rowan Scott) — if she breaks cleanly and immediately goes unchallenged to the front, monitor whether the prominent trio (Wait Geordie, Undercover Affair, Seed Ya Later) apply any early pressure or gift her a soft lead that could prove decisive.

Wait Geordie's OR 80 is the highest in the field but Jack Callan takes 3lbs off; watch whether the claimer settles him into a smooth prominent position or whether the weight advantage is undermined by early positional errors in a race with multiple prominent types converging.

Undercover Affair's visor (headgear flag) could sharpen her at the break and see her race keenly — if she over-travels in the first two furlongs trying to press Past Passion, her finishing effort in the closing stages may be compromised.

Holi Scarlett and On The Queue Tee (both genuine hold-up types) will be tracking from the rear in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to bring them into it — watch whether there is any clear rail or far-side channel opening late for either to exploit.

The going report confirms this 5f strip is Good to Firm despite the card listing Good — fast ground compresses finishing times and tends to reward those with early position, reinforcing the prominent-runner advantage identified in the pace map.

races.name: Construction Day 14th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Al Maslool
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained hold-up horse for Cieren Fallon, 14 days since last run and wearing a hood; four runs on good ground returning 0W1P but showed a solid third at Sandown — the class yard and top jockey booking are the primary angles here, with his natural style suiting this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Produced his best recent form when runner-up at Lingfield on his latest start, having been tried over a longer distance; drops back to 10f here again in cheekpieces and, if he builds on that effort, his rating gives him sound claims at the head of this field.

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race and the likely pace-setter by default; Clifford Lee rides for Ollie Sangster whose stable has gone 0/24 over the past 14 days, and crucially this horse's single win came on soft, not the good-to-firm conditions on offer today — the going is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Landed her first win in a handicap by half a length at Ffos Las on her latest start, showing real resolve in the process; faces a 3lb higher mark on quicker ground today and the trainer's current form is a slight caveat.

runners_data.name: Red Rifle
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's lightly-raced hold-up type recorded a convincing 1m2f win on good ground 20 days ago and steps up in class; the 14f win on good is the best distance-going match in the field, making this a horse to respect at a potentially generous price.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten over a marathon trip on his latest outing when the extended distance proved beyond him, but that run counts for little; the return to 10f is much more his domain and he arrives 1lb lower with a trainer in good form, having landed a race in his recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ceinture d'Orion
runners_data.note: David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope combine with a horse whose true race style is held up at the rear; placed on good ground and drops back to a trip that suits, though the style-fit tag means his chance is tempered if he is pushed forward — the trainer's 6/56 recent record keeps him in the picture.
runners_data.comment: Third at a mile in a novice at Ripon on her latest run, a trip shorter than she handles best, and this return to 10f in handicap company looks a positive angle; without a win in recent starts but she enters this sphere with genuine potential and could progress.

runners_data.name: Emma's Letter
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's filly returns from a 52-day absence wearing a hood and has bumped into rivals at shorter trips; placed on good ground over 1m2f and 1m, but the layoff and a natural tendency to race held-up means she needs a clean passage — a genuine hold-up type shuffled forward on the map.
runners_data.comment: Tendency to race keenly held her back when well beaten at Windsor on her latest outing; returns after a short break with first-time blinkers fitted, which may help settle her, though she is yet to prove she stays 10f and faces a stiff task at the weights.

runners_data.name: Baron Wagstaff
runners_data.note: Richard Phillips runner back after 78 days off — the long absence is the dominant concern; has only three career runs and goes 0W0P on similar going, and Sean Bowen's switch from jumps to the flat adds further uncertainty here despite the positive trainer stat context being absent (0/4).
runners_data.comment: Keen and well below par in a novice at Southwell on his latest start, making no impression there; absent for 78 days and steps into handicap company for the first time, though he is bred for middle-distances and may do better in this sphere with experience.

runners_data.name: Bergamo Gold
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's consistent type comes off a 45-day break with a solid 113298 form string including wins and places on soft and standard; however, good-to-firm is unproven territory based on his single run on good returning a disappointing 8th, and his true hold-up style makes him reliant on pace developing in front.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins in her recent starts came on all-weather surfaces and her turf ability is unproven, which is the clear obstacle today; gave nothing in the closing stages when well beaten at Redcar on her latest outing and remains hard to trust here.

races.paceDynamic: Liveinthelight is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this seven-runner 1m2f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no rival likely to press for the lead, the fractions will be controlled and sustainable rather than end-to-end. The remainder of the field — Al Maslool, Red Rifle, Ceinture d'Orion, Emma's Letter, Baron Wagstaff and Bergamo Gold — are all natural hold-up types, meaning Liveinthelight should enjoy a genuinely uncontested lead and set a rhythm entirely on its own terms. This race shape strongly favours horses capable of travelling powerfully through the race from midfield and finishing with purpose, as the steady tempo will compress the field and make a late burst the decisive factor. Several runners — Ceinture d'Orion, Emma's Letter, Baron Wagstaff and Bergamo Gold — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all race at the rear and have been mapped forward on the visual; those most likely to actually secure their natural position are the ones drawn or ridden to drop in quietly, but the redistribution means the race shape remains dominated by closers who must pick their way through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Liveinthelight Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Liveinthelight dictates a steady gallop unchallenged and the field closes evenly in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Liveinthelight dictates a steady gallop unchallenged and the field closes evenly in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Pounce Decisively
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the hold-up horses get clear runs in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the hold-up horses get clear runs in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Liveinthelight Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Liveinthelight's jockey Clifford Lee presses on turning for home and the hold-up pack is caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If Liveinthelight's jockey Clifford Lee presses on turning for home and the hold-up pack is caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Problems Shuffle Result
scenarios.trigger: If bunching behind a slow pace creates interference and those with wide draws or clean passage benefit unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: If bunching behind a slow pace creates interference and those with wide draws or clean passage benefit unexpectedly.

watchPoints.text: Liveinthelight sets an uncontested lead — watch whether Clifford Lee presses on turning for home, as any significant quickening mid-race will expose every hold-up runner in this field simultaneously.

With five natural hold-up types all needing to produce their challenge in the straight, monitor early positioning — significant bunching or interference in the final two furlongs is a genuine risk that could blindside fancied runners.

Al Maslool's hood (hg:p) is noted and Cieren Fallon's booking is the headline positive angle — watch whether the hood produces a more tractable early effort that allows him to travel smoothly through a compressed field.

Red Rifle's recent 1m2f win on good ground is the strongest form-to-condition match in the race; watch his price in the market as a potential underlay or overlay depending on how punters assess the class rise.
Emma's Letter's 52-day absence combined with the hood (hg:b) means an early behavioral read in the paddock and at the start is worth tracking before committing to any view on her chance.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Thornaby Annie
runners_data.note: Improved hold-up filly who has placed twice at 7-8f on good ground recently; the step to 1m½f looks a stretch for a horse who has raced almost exclusively at 6-7f, but good-going form is solid and Jack Nicholls claiming allowance helps offset the weight; 17 days fresh.
runners_data.comment: Opened her account in a handicap at Wetherby last time, landing a neck success over a mile on good to firm ground; arrives here wearing a first-time hood off a slightly higher mark, and she handles both trip and conditions well — she looks well placed on the revised figure.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Billy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile whose form figures of 2-8-4 on good-to-firm offer limited encouragement; best efforts have come at 8f on softer ground and the combination of this trip and fast conditions is untested, making this a speculative runner for Jessica Macey's yard who have not fired from 9 recent runners.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back and handles a mile on good ground; pulled freely at Newbury last time when beaten 4 lengths, which makes first-time cheekpieces today of interest as an aid to settle him — yet to score in recent starts but not without a chance on his best.

runners_data.name: Storm Esme
runners_data.note: The race's only natural front-runner and key pace influence; Tim Easterby's filly won over 6f on good ground but now faces 1m½f — a significant jump in trip — which is the central question mark; if she gets to the front uncontested she is dangerous, but her best form has come in shorter, sharper contests.
runners_data.comment: Won earlier in her recent starts and her latest run at Ayr — beaten 8 lengths over 7f — showed a hint of returning form despite the beaten margin; effective on varied surfaces and with her mark on a downward trend, she merits respect if recapturing that earlier level.

runners_data.name: Empirical
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's hold-up performer has shown ability at 8f on good ground (third twice); pushed into a mapped midfield position given the congestion of rear-runners, but his natural instinct is to settle and finish, and at 54 days off, fitness is the genuine question; Cieren Fallon's booking is an upgrade.
runners_data.comment: Placed third on his handicap debut here last time, beaten just 1 1/2 lengths off this same mark, and handles today's trip and going well; wears cheekpieces and looks to have more to offer — the top-rated runner in the field and the one to be with.

runners_data.name: Sahara Magic
runners_data.note: A consistent backmarker whose seven recent finishes have all come in the 6th-to-7th range, suggesting a horse that competes without threatening; Michael Appleby has two winners from 13 recent runners but Sahara Magic's form offers little to build a case on, and she is placed into a midfield role she would not naturally adopt.
runners_data.comment: Consistently finishing in the lower half of the field in recent starts, beaten 7 lengths at Carlisle last time while failing to respond when asked; effective over 6f on AW but today's mile on turf poses a stamina question, and more is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Albertini Star
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant concern in a race where late running is paramount; 218 days absent is a major fitness worry, and Alan King's 4/11 recent yard form does not compensate; Clifford Lee inherits a horse whose three runs show a declining trajectory from 8th to 6th to 10th.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for over seven months since a below-par effort at Southwell, and sits last on our ratings; wears a first-time hood today and the trainer is in good form, which offers some encouragement — but the long absence means she is taken on trust.

runners_data.name: Mereside Princess
runners_data.note: Arrives in the best recent form of any runner with back-to-back wins at 8f on good and soft ground; her hg=b (blinkers) suggests she has been sharpened up by headgear, and while she is a true hold-up type shuffled forward on the map by circumstance, her genuine class edge over these rivals and William Pyle's local experience make her the form pick regardless of positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last six starts and beaten only a nose last time off this same mark of 62, showing real tenacity; arrives today wearing first-time blinkers and handles the trip and going — a consistent filly who rates a genuine threat to our top pick.

runners_data.name: Kameko Fever
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's hold-up performer has placed at 8f on good ground and is 10 days off a run, so fitness is not a concern; Oisin Orr is a significant jockey booking and the horse's consistent placing (two fourths, a second) suggests reliability without a finishing burst, making a front-running position — which the map redistributes her into — somewhat artificial.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Musselburgh last time but showed considerably more in earlier recent starts, including a runner-up effort; suited by a mile on a sound surface, he arrives today wearing first-time cheekpieces — a bounce-back is needed but not without some claims on better form.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Esme is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m½f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no genuine pace rival to press her, David Allan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style — Empirical, Sahara Magic, Albertini Star, Mereside Princess and Kameko Fever are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many rear-of-field types to accommodate; of those, Mereside Princess and Kameko Fever are most likely to secure a forward position given their recent prominent-tracking form hints. With one honest pace-setter over a flat mile and a furlong, this race shape is set to favour hold-up horses with a genuine, sustained late run — provided they can access a clear passage from what will likely be a tight, bunched mid-race pack — though the redistribution caveat means many of those closers are not natural sit-and-sprint types and may not fully capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Storm Esme Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a true but not extravagant gallop that the hold-up pack cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: If Storm Esme is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a true but not extravagant gallop that the hold-up pack cannot reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough to string out the field and two or three hold-up horses find clear runs to deliver sustained late challenges.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves just quick enough to string out the field and two or three hold-up horses find clear runs to deliver sustained late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme is tracked closely by Mereside Princess or Kameko Fever and the pace lifts in the final quarter-mile, exposing the front-runner.
scenarios.body: If Storm Esme is tracked closely by Mereside Princess or Kameko Fever and the pace lifts in the final quarter-mile, exposing the front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Stragglers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme sets a falsely slow early gallop and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If Storm Esme sets a falsely slow early gallop and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.

watchPoints.text: Storm Esme must be tracked from flag-fall — if David Allan is allowed to stride clear unchallenged by the two-furlong pole, hold-up horses face a tough ask on this flat track with limited time to close.

Mereside Princess is the standout form horse but carries blinkers and is a natural hold-up type mapped forward; watch whether William Pyle attempts to track Storm Esme or drops her out, as her positional choice will heavily influence her winning chance.
Albertini Star's 218-day absence combined with a tendency to fade in the finish makes her a significant in-running drift risk — if she shows early, expect her to weaken inside the final two furlongs.

The bunching of six genuine hold-up horses in the mid-to-rear section means a traffic problem in the straight is likely; horses drawn widest (Kameko Fever, Empirical) may have the clearest run but face the longest route around.

Good-to-firm conditions confirmed for the 4:05 — any horse whose best form has come on softer ground (Mayflower Billy, Storm Esme's soft-ground win) should be slightly downgraded relative to those with proven good-ground credentials like Thornaby Annie and Mereside Princess.

races.name: Wildwest Beer Festival 4th July Handicap

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a win and a place in similar going at 8f, now stepping up to 10f which the form suggests it handles; 12 days since last run is sharp enough, and the 3/10f Good placed run in history is an encouraging pointer for this trip.
runners_data.comment: Missed the kick at Newmarket last time and never threatened from the rear; today's first-time tongue-tie is of note and he has placed in recent starts, suggesting ability, but he needs things to fall right over this trip and makes more appeal as a speculative each-way entry.

runners_data.name: Crimson Road
runners_data.note: William Carson takes the ride on this hold-up performer returning from a 56-day break, and the longer trip profile (placed at 17f) suggests stamina is not an issue even if current form at 8f has been modest; Good to Firm going is well-suited on a 12/15 similar-going record.
runners_data.comment: Stays 8-10f on a sound surface and returns after a break of nearly two months; his most recent run on the Flat at Windsor was below par, and more is needed before he can get competitive with this type of company — his mark has been falling but further improvement is required.

runners_data.name: Spec Of Light
runners_data.note: Strong on form figures over staying trips on Standard ground but the sim-going record is just 2/15 on Good to Firm, raising a significant surface concern; carries its role as a natural closer but finds itself pushed toward midfield in a field over-subscribed with hold-up types, reducing the chance of getting ideal cover.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and in a difficult spell at present; his most recent outing saw him run too keenly over an excessive distance at Wolverhampton, and while he handles 8-12f and is effective on AW, he needs to rediscover form to land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Beauty Generation
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed form at 10f in both Good and Standard going, showing consistent mid-division efforts; a true hold-up performer who will likely find itself more prominent than preferred given the sheer volume of closers in this race, which compromises its natural game.
runners_data.comment: In solid form prior to a well-below-par run at Leicester last time, and the trainer is currently going well; wears first-time cheekpieces today and is effective over 8-12f on a sound surface — if that Leicester effort can be excused, he rates a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Rugby Union
runners_data.note: The form flag for fading in the finish is a material concern at 1m2f on Good to Firm; a hold-up-style three-year-old from a yard that has been running at a modest 1/15 over 14 days, and the step up from 7f to 10f makes this a demanding assignment.
runners_data.comment: Returned to near his best at Wetherby last time, beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a mark 1lb above today's, and handles 10f on good to firm ground; yet to score in recent starts but the form is moving in the right direction — further improvement is expected.

runners_data.name: Mohmentous
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — recent back-to-back wins over 8f on Good and Firm demonstrate genuine tactical speed, and Tudhope's booking is a significant upgrade; as the lone front-runner it can dictate entirely, though it is technically racing in a prominent role and carries a STYLE_FIT note that tempers any complacency about holding on.
runners_data.comment: Two wins from his last six starts and only beaten 2 lengths at short odds last time off this same mark; the step up to 10f could bring out more and he looks well treated on a mark that reflects his ability — the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Talking In Kode
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner with a placed run at 8f in Good going and consistent efforts at this track and trip; Cian Horgan's 5lb claim helps at the weights, and the hood (hg:p) suggests the trainer has found a route to getting its best, though winning form over this configuration remains elusive.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 8 lengths at Leicester last time when unable to find any acceleration, but the step up to 10f today could prove more suitable; wears first-time cheekpieces and acts on good to firm — needs to find more on current form to feature but the trip change offers hope.

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this three-year-old with placed form at 8f on Firm ground — genuinely relevant for today's conditions — but as a natural closer it will be shuffled into midfield rather than its preferred deep hold-up spot, which Fallon will need to manage carefully from barrier.
runners_data.comment: In decent form earlier in the year and handles varied going from soft to firm over 7-9f; his latest at Ffos Las was modest, beaten 6 1/4 lengths, and he wears a tongue-tie today — yet to score in recent starts but place claims are possible on a return to form.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Geisha
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is in strong form (6/54 over 14 days) and this three-year-old has four placed efforts from six at 10f in Good going, making it one of the most consistent profiles in the race for this trip and surface; despite being a true closer mapped forward due to field composition, the 9-day turnaround indicates fitness and the 10f Good form is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just a short-head at Beverley last time off this same mark, showing real consistency throughout her career; stays 10f and acts well on fast ground — yet to score but holds a manageable official rating and her persistence makes her a genuine danger.

races.paceDynamic: Mohmentous is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, Daniel Tudhope can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f Nottingham flat on Good to Firm ground. Talking In Kode is the only other prominent-style runner and will track Mohmentous, but there is no pressure likely to force a genuinely hot pace — this sets up as a classic single-pace-setter scenario. The remaining seven runners are all natural hold-up types, yet the field is so loaded with closers that Spec Of Light, Phantom Shadow, Beauty Generation and Wadacre Geisha have been redistributed to midfield on the map, as their true rear-running positions are oversubscribed — in reality several of these will not find the deep cover they prefer. A single uncontested pace-setter on a flat track in Good to Firm conditions typically compresses the race into one sustained rhythm with no significant acceleration change, which firmly favours a horse who can sit close to the gallop and outstay rivals rather than one needing a sprint finish from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mohmentous Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mohmentous leads without pressure and Tudhope controls the tempo throughout, the race becomes a stamina test from the front.
scenarios.body: If Mohmentous leads without pressure and Tudhope controls the tempo throughout, the race becomes a stamina test from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Hit Form
scenarios.trigger: If Mohmentous sets an honest enough gallop that closers can reel him in over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Mohmentous sets an honest enough gallop that closers can reel him in over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Mohmentous and Talking In Kode break cleanly and the rest of the field is left flat-footed in a steady-run race that never truly tests staying power.
scenarios.body: If Mohmentous and Talking In Kode break cleanly and the rest of the field is left flat-footed in a steady-run race that never truly tests staying power.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Unlocks Value
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race or the genuine 10f distance trips up the shorter-trip specialists, rewarding proven stayers.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens mid-race or the genuine 10f distance trips up the shorter-trip specialists, rewarding proven stayers.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mohmentous at the start — if Tudhope secures the lead cleanly and unchallenged, the controlled tempo this creates means the race is likely over before the straight.

Watch Wadacre Geisha's position in the early stages; if Connor Beasley can slot in just off the pace rather than being buried at the rear, the consistent 10f Good form gives it a genuine winning chance in most scenarios.
Talking In Kode with the hood on bears watching for any signs of keenness behind the leader — if it gets loose and burns energy early, it becomes far less effective over the final two furlongs.

Spec Of Light's sim-going record of just 2/15 on turf Good-to-Firm is a red flag worth monitoring in running — if it appears laboured before the final bend, the surface may simply be too quick for it regardless of race shape.

Rugby Union's finishing-fade flag makes it worth watching whether it is still travelling at the two-furlong pole; any sign of weakening before that point confirms the trip and going combination is beyond it today.

races.name: Events At Nottingham Racecourse Training Series Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact 5f trip on Good ground which is significant form, but is a natural hold-up type who will be squeezed closer to the pace than ideal by this race's shape; trainer Easterby 14-day record modest, and the redistribution away from the rear is the key risk to her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth beaten four lengths on a mark 1lb higher than today when marginally below her best on her latest start, and she has shown she can compete at this level in recent starts; a return to that form would make her a factor, though a step forward is still required.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Has headgear noted and shows consistent form at 5f on various surfaces, though none of her recent five runs have come on Good to Firm which is today's confirmed going; a true closer by style who will struggle to find her preferred position at the back in this seven-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last four starts and performed to expectation when fourth at Beverley on his latest outing, off a mark 1lb higher than today; equipped with first-time cheekpieces here and heads this field on our ratings, with 5f on a sound surface clearly his best conditions.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with 15 of last 15 runs on Good ground so has no going concern, but recent form shows a string of mid-to-rear finishes and no win in the last five; naturally a hold-up operator who may be boxed in closer to the pace than suits, and trainer has a flat 0/5 over the last 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ripon on her most recent start in a manner that suggested she was not at her best that day; handles 5f on a sound surface and has shown better form at this trip, but the last two outings give little grounds for confidence.

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: Highest rated runner in the field on paper at OR 73 but recent form is woeful — six, 17, 17, eight, nine — and the apprentice claiming seven pounds cannot mask that the horse is simply out of sorts; hold-up style maps him to the back of this small field where he needs chaos to feature.|
runners_data.comment: Suited by five furlongs on a sound surface and holds a fair official rating, suggesting latent ability; failed to land a blow from well off the pace at Redcar last time and the trainer is going through a lean patch, so a considerable improvement in form is required.

runners_data.name: Beaumadier
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-racer who sits naturally just off the pace, which is exactly the tactical position this race shape rewards; 0/18 for trainer Loughnane over the last 14 days is a mild concern, and only 1 of 15 recent runs has come on Good going, yet pattern form at 5f includes a win and multiple places.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to his best when a close third at Thirsk on his latest start, inclined to pull hard but still going down by just a length and a half off a 1lb higher mark; effective at 5f on a range of surfaces, though the inconsistency in his profile remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Won twice in last six starts including a course win at 5f on Good going and a 6f win, giving him the most relevant positional form in the field; despite a hold-up style he is well-handicapped at OR 75 and if he can race handier than usual on this flat, sharp track the profile is compelling.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth despite an untidy exit from the stalls on his latest outing, a run that belies his ability at this trip on good to firm ground; arrives on the same mark with two wins in his recent starts and can go well once more at 5f.

runners_data.name: Sam's Hope
runners_data.note: The lone front runner with a prominent tag and a clear tactical role as sole pace-setter; has the highest official rating (OR 75) but all five recent runs have been on Standard or soft surfaces and only 1 of 15 runs comes on Good going, which is a meaningful concern on today's Good to Firm ground — 62 days off adds uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Off a mark 1lb higher than today on her latest run and beaten three and a half lengths, the reduction in grade here is an advantage; returns with a first-time tongue-tie after 62 days off the track and handles 5f on a sound surface.

races.paceDynamic: Sam's Hope is the sole confirmed front runner and, with only Beaumadier likely to press from a prominent position, should be able to control the tempo on Good to Firm ground over this flat 5f at Nottingham without facing any serious early challenge. That creates a genuinely sustainable pace — not a crawl, but measured enough that Sam's Hope can dictate rhythm and avoid burning out the leader's stamina advantage. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse that can sit just off the front and pick up in the final furlong, as the prominent-to-mid profile is where the tactical edge lies under this scenario. This field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate — Miss Brazen, Spirit Of Applause, and Hurt You Never are genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than is natural for them, diluting the benefit of any late finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sam's Hope Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Hope leads uncontested and Beaumadier sits a length or two adrift without mounting any real early pressure.
scenarios.body: If Sam's Hope leads uncontested and Beaumadier sits a length or two adrift without mounting any real early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Hope sets a slightly stronger pace than ideal and Winchurch, racing handier than its typical hold-up style, lands a decisive blow in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Sam's Hope sets a slightly stronger pace than ideal and Winchurch, racing handier than its typical hold-up style, lands a decisive blow in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Hope overcooks the early pace and the true hold-up horses find more room to close than the race shape typically allows.
scenarios.body: If Sam's Hope overcooks the early pace and the true hold-up horses find more room to close than the race shape typically allows.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break fast, crowding the early pace picture and turning the race into a sprint where no one settles cleanly.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses break fast, crowding the early pace picture and turning the race into a sprint where no one settles cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Sam's Hope's going suitability is a live risk — only 1 of 15 career runs on Good going and today is confirmed Good to Firm, so monitor closely whether the horse handles the faster surface before assigning it full weight in any scenario.

Beaumadier's trainer Loughnane has a 0/18 strike rate over the past 14 days; while the horse fits the race shape perfectly, the trainer's current cold run is worth factoring against it at shorter odds.

Miss Brazen, Spirit Of Applause, and Hurt You Never are all genuine hold-up types who cannot all settle at the back of a seven-runner field — watch how they break and whether any of them ends up chasing the pace uncomfortably, which would compromise their late-run entirely.

Winchurch is the only runner with a confirmed win at this exact 5f Nottingham trip on Good going and has won twice recently — if the pace scenario produces any weakness in the front two, it is the horse most likely to arrive with a decisive challenge.
